Briefings in Bioinformatics.title: Transformer models in genomics: from sequence analysis to population genetics and biodiversity
Briefings in Bioinformatics.abstract: AbstractModern genomics and artificial intelligence converge at a breakthrough point with the emergence of transformer-based large language models for genomic analysis. This review examines how transformer-based models have advanced genomic sequence analysis through novel tokenization strategies, self-attention mechanisms, and pre-training/fine-tuning paradigms. Unlike prior broad surveys, we focus on three sub-areas of genomics where transformer architectures have had a substantive impact: sequence-level analysis, population-level genetics, including genetic imputation and genome-wide association analysis, and biodiversity research, while addressing challenges like genome-scale computational demands, training biases, and interpreting attention in biological contexts. Looking forward, we outline how emerging foundation models, multi-modal integration, and biologically informed attention mechanisms could transform our understanding of genome function, providing a roadmap for leveraging genome language models to decode genome complexity and advance functional and population-level genomics.

Water Research.title: The performance of one-stage PNA process coupled with nitrate removal-targeted electrochemical unit.
Water Research.abstract: During the operation of the one-stage partial nitritation/anammox (PNA) process, nitrate is the inevitable product, which not only limits the total nitrogen removal efficiency (NRE), but also brings the burden of post-denitrification treatment. Electrochemical nitrate reduction is a potentially effective route for nitrate removal with merits such as no second pollution and sludge production. Therefore, in this study, for the first time, a one-stage PNA-electrochemical (EC) unit system, with Cu(I)/Cu(II) oxide nanowires as the cathode for nitrate removal and IrO₂-Ta₂O₅/Ti mesh as the anode, was developed. The results showed that the EC unit worked well with PNA process under proper condition, finally NRE of the whole system reached 84.1 ± 2.0%, and the effluent nitrate concentration was markedly lower than the theoretical value with the maximum nitrate reduction efficiency reached 45.8%. Moreover, the electroactive denitrifiers (Denitratisoma and Brevundimonas) and the hydrogenotrophic denitrifier (Hydrogenophaga) were detected in the system. Both theoretical analysis and separate batch experiments indicated that nitrate was mainly converted into nitrite attributed to the electrochemical nitrate reduction and the hydrogenotrophic denitrification. Notably the external aeration demand decreased by approximately 41%, which was likely attributed to the oxygen released from anodic oxygen evolution reaction. These findings together indicate a synergistic interaction between the biological process and electrochemical process. Overall, coupling one-stage PNA with EC unit is promising in enabling the effective removal of nitrate produced during the PNA process and potentially paving the way to overcome the NRE limit of PNA process. This novel process also gives a reference for addressing the intrinsic limitation of other anammox-based processes.

Genome Biology.title: Human astrocyte aging couples chromatin closure to focal G-quadruplex accumulation
Genome Biology.abstract: Background Aging disrupts genome organization and transcriptional fidelity, but the role of non-canonical DNA structures remains unclear. G-quadruplexes (G4s) are stable, guanine-rich DNA and RNA structures that regulate gene expression and genome integrity. However, their contribution to aging remains unknown. Here, we examine age-associated changes in G4 abundance, chromatin accessibility, and G4-helicase DDX5 expression in human astrocytes established from the brain resections of donors spanning early to late adulthood and expanded in culture before analysis. Results Imaging with N-TASQ and BG4 shows increased G4 signal in astrocytes from older donors, together with reduced nuclear DDX5 expression. ATAC-seq profiling reveals an age-associated decline in chromatin accessibilityat intergenic, intronic, and promoter-proximal regions. Genome-wide mapping of G4s by G4 CUT&Tag identifies focal enrichment at specific loci in older astrocytes, including sites within both accessible and less accessible chromatin. We overexpress DDX5 in young astrocytes and observe transcriptional changes in pathways associated with chromatin organization, genome maintenance, stress signaling, and synaptic function. In contrast, acute DDX5 depletion causes focal G4 accumulation without reproducing broader chromatin changes observed with aging. Conclusions This study defines an age-associated axis in human astrocytes that links reduced DDX5, focal G4 abundance, and progressive loss of chromatin accessibility. Our findings identify G4 regulation as a candidate mechanism shaping genome control during astrocyte aging.

eLife.title: Endocardial TIE1 synergizes with TIE2 to regulate the atrial internal muscular network assembly
eLife.abstract: Atrial cardiomyopathy is characterized by altered atrial structures, yet its underlying genetic basis remains inadequately explored. TIE1 mutations are reported in lymphedema patients, but whether they exhibit cardiac defects alongside lymphatic abnormalities remains unknown. Here, single-cell RNA sequencing showed high Tie1 and Tek expression in atrial endocardial cells. TIE1 deficiency severely disrupted atrial morphogenesis, with only minor ventricular defects. Bulk RNA-seq showed reduced transcripts for endothelial development and cardiac trabeculation in Tie1 mutants. Separate RNA-seq analysis of the atria and ventricles further confirmed these findings, revealing a more pronounced downregulation of trabecular genes, including Tek, in the atria upon Tie1 loss. Endothelial deletion of Tek impaired trabeculation, particularly in atria. Consistently, Tie1 loss combined with a single null Tek allele disrupted both atrial and ventricular trabeculation. Strikingly, atrial morphogenesis defects appeared within 48 hr of induced endothelial Tie1 loss coupled with Tek heterozygous deletion, implying a critical endocardial role in organizing the atrial muscular network. The synergy of TIE1 and TIE2 in remodeling atrial trabeculae was confirmed postnatally, whereas TIE1 insufficiency alone had no obvious effect. Together, TIE1 is differentially required for atrial versus ventricular development, acting synergistically with TIE2 to regulate endocardial cell-coordinated assembly of atrial internal muscular network.
